newsitem.title: USA: Dole campaign fundraiser sentenced, fined.
newsitem.headline: Dole campaign fundraiser sentenced, fined.

text.p: An aide to a former vice chairman of the Bob Dole presidential campaign finance committee pleaded guilty on Monday to fraud and conspiracy and was sentenced to four months of home confinement.

Carol Ann Nichols, who worked for the privately held Avon, Mass.-based Aqua-Leisure company, admitted that between 1991 and 1995, she helped her boss, Simon Fireman, funnel more than $120,000 to several campaigns.

The Dole presidential bid received the lion's share of the illicit funds, prosecutors said, adding that the Republican National Committee, the Citizens for Joe Kennedy Committee and the Bush-Quayle '92 campaign also received funds.

U.S. District Judge William Young accepted her guilty plea to conspiracy and fraud charges and sentenced her to one year probation with the first four months to be served in home confinement. She was also ordered to pay a $7,500 fine.
Young sentenced Fireman on Oct. 23 to six months of home confinement and ordered him to pay a $1 million fine. His sporting goods company was ordered to pay a $5 million fine.

Fireman, with Nichols' help, set up a secret trust in the United States with funds wired from Hong Kong. The money was then given to Aqua-Leisure employees who would write checks for between $1,000 and $4,000 to the various campaigns.
